**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding**: no standardised first-touch, induction, or goal-setting process; retention bleeds hardest in weeks 1–4
- **Churn & Cancellation**: no documented reason-capture, win-back trigger, or exit interview protocol
- **Member Check-ins**: no scheduled touchpoint cadence (30/60/90 day) or conversation framework to identify at-risk members early
- **Coaching Development & Standards**: no defined progression path for coaches or quality audit framework; inconsistent delivery across classes
- **Class Quality Audit**: no mechanism to measure coaching consistency, cueing, form correction, or member experience week-to-week
- **Referral Programme**: no structure, incentive tier, or tracking system despite word-of-mouth being your cheapest acquisition
- **Health & Safety Incident Log**: no protocol for documenting injuries, near-misses, or complaints; legal/insurance exposure
- **GDPR & Member Data Privacy**: no documented data handling, consent, retention, or deletion process
- **Supply Chain (Order Supplies & Sundries)**: no stock, reorder, or vendor management SOP; impacts studio cleanliness and experience
- **Pause & Resumption**: no clear eligibility, duration limits, re-engagement process, or follow-up sequence

**Needs updating**

- **Coaches SOPs (20 built)**: likely missing detail on how to adapt class for mixed-ability cohorts; no escalation path for members struggling with form or confidence
- **Marketing SOPs (5 built)**: no integration with retention/win-back campaigns; onboarding and referral programs likely orphaned from comms calendar
- **Facilities (5 built)**: missing daily/weekly deep-clean checklists, equipment maintenance logs, and emergency procedures (power failure, injury, evacuation)

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO ACTIONS

## REVENUE — CRITICAL PRIORITY

- **Churn spike & member leakage**: July shows 151 active clients but only £1,363 revenue—that's AR/M of £9.03, down 92% from June's £120.48. You're carrying ghost members who aren't paying. Audit the 151 roster immediately: are inactive members still counted? Lock in payment terms (direct debit mandate enforcement) and run a re-engagement campaign on lapsed payers within 7 days.

- **Pricing cliff**: Pre-relocation (Sep–Nov) your AR/M ranged £128–£162; post-relocation (May–July) it's erratic (£165 → £120 → £9). The bigger studio should support premium pricing and larger cohorts. Raise base membership price by 8–12% (from estimated £120–160 to £130–180/month) and introduce a "premium tier" (dedicated locker + peak-hour class priority) at +£15/month. Test on new sign-ups first.

- **New revenue lines underdeveloped**: At 151 members, you have no PT sessions, merchandise, nutrition plans, or corporate partnerships listed. Add 1–2 PT slots per week (£40–50/session, 50% margin) and a basic supplement/apparel retail display (20% margin, zero capex). Target £500/month by August.

- **June profitability (5.28%) to July revenue collapse is unexplained**: Investigate: payment processing failures, invoice timing shifts, or one-off member departure. If systemic, implement weekly revenue reporting (not just monthly) starting immediately.

---

## EXPENSES — STAFFING & UTILITIES

- **Non-people costs have spiralled**: June £9,390 → July £701 suggests either a reporting error or April's fit-out costs are still being absorbed. Clarify: are utilities, insurance, and rent properly allocated monthly, or backloaded? Expect stable ~£4,500/month run-rate for the larger space. If June included one-off costs, that's fine; but lock a fixed 12-month facility budget and audit supplier contracts (rent, utilities, insurance) for the new premises—you should be paying for the extra space, not double.

- **People costs creeping**: September–November averaged £2,598; May–July averaged £3,579 (+38%). You've added staff for the bigger studio—justified—but monitor: are you at optimal FTE for 151 members? Benchmark: 1 manager + 2 instructors should serve

# Concrete Execution for Service Menu Creation

• **Split into two documents NOW, not one:** Coaches see pricing architecture + commission structure + what they're allowed to upsell. Members see clean pricing + what's bundled (e.g., "unlimited classes + 2 nutrition calls/month = £49"). This prevents coaches saying different things to different people.

• **Audit what you're actually selling first:** Walk the gym for 2 hours. List every service a member could buy (class, PT session, nutrition chat, merchandise, guest pass). You probably have 8-12 things people assume are included that aren't, or vice versa. Clarify before you publish anything.

• **Price by outcome, not just time:** Don't say "30-min PT = £35." Say "Get your form dialed in for 3 lifts = £35." Members buy results. This also makes it easier to justify pricing to coaches who get asked "why is it this much?"

• **Post the member version in 3 places:** Printed A4 at reception, downloadable PDF on your site, and as an Instagram carousel (broken into 3-4 slides). Coaches get their version laminated at their station. No "we'll email it later"—it lives where people ask questions.

• **Update this every 90 days minimum:** Prices change, offerings shift. Set a calendar reminder. Nothing kills trust faster than outdated menus or coaches quoting old rates.

What's your current list of services people actually pay for?

## REVENUE — INCREASE IT

• **Membership price is too low.** Rev/member averaged £124–131 across Jan–Jun, jumped to £129 in July but sits well below potential. At 153 active members, you're leaving £8–15/month per member on the table. Test a £5–8 price rise on new joiners this month; existing members on legacy rates drag the average down. Target: £145 Rev/member by Q4.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** — your second-worst month on record. Investigate what happened then (staffing change? class cancellations? marketing drop?). July sits at 7.9%, which is acceptable, but you need churn consistently under 5% to compound growth. Implement a member check-in/NPS survey this month to find friction early.

• **You've grown from 111 to 153 members in 7 months (+38%) but July revenue only £19,764** — that's just +25% vs Dec 2025. Member growth is real, pricing is the gap. Upsell personal training, nutrition plans, or merchandise bundles at point of sale; margin on add-ons will be 60%+ vs 40% on membership.

• **Off-peak class capacity is the next frontier.** You don't report occupancy by time slot, but with 153 members and (presumably) morning/lunchtime/evening classes, weekday mornings and early afternoons are likely half-full. Offer a discount for off-peak-only membership (£35/month vs standard £55) to fill dead slots without cannibalising premium members. Target: +15 members in quiet slots by September.

Rule: expenses should track revenue within 5–10%, not 20%.
